decisions.reason: Variation B retains the already-established shared baseline; the client's selection confirms rather than changes the baseline rule.
The separate E/L height instruction in message 171 is already captured by a complete same-message MODIFY; the kerning selection requires no additional E/L update.
Selecting the tighter kerning variation does not alter the all-caps case treatment.
The proof already supplied the requested comparison variations; selecting Variation B changes the product's kerning choice, not the proof-format requirement.
The separate height-hierarchy change in message 171 is already represented by a complete same-message MODIFY; tighter kerning adds no further hierarchy change.
The client selects a kerning variation but does not add it to the locked assets or change the revision-preservation policy.
The kerning selection does not modify the Hero V's geometry or its architectural role.
Message 171 does not change how the second V is constructed; it adjusts surrounding E/L scale and selects kerning.
The request to verify an exact copy/paste reiterates the existing literal-derivation rule and does not change its value.
The kerning choice has no effect on the deferred champagne-metal material treatment.
Message 171 requests verification of accent geometry but does not change the established Hero V–accent peak-alignment rule.
